content.text: {"relation": "REFINED", "consensus_summary": "Consensus: leaven predominantly symbolizes sin, corruption, hypocrisy, or false teaching whose defining trait is pervasive spread through the whole, grounded in Passover removal (Ex 12), the exclusion from offerings (Lev 2:11), Jesus' warnings about the leaven of the Pharisees (Matt 16:6-12; Luke 12:1), and Paul's 'a little leaven leavens the whole lump' (1 Cor 5:6-8; Gal 5:9). A common, well-recognized alternative reads the parable of the leaven (Matt 13:33) positively as the kingdom's hidden growth; a minority reads even that negatively; some treat leaven as a neutral image of pervasive influence.", "book_summary": "The book identifies leaven as 'bread soured' — since bread symbolizes the word (cross-referenced to the Grass chapter), leaven is the word made impure, embittered, and puffed up: hidden corruption fermenting through the whole lump, purged before Passover and forbidden on the altar, and named in the NT as the corrupt doctrine of the Pharisees.", "consensus_core_identification": "Leaven = sin/corruption/false teaching/hypocrisy that spreads pervasively through the whole (with an acknowledged positive kingdom-growth usage as a secondary sense).", "book_core_identification": "Leaven = corruption of the word/doctrine specifically — soured bread as the impure, puffed-up word, epitomized in the corrupt doctrine of the Pharisees.", "core_relation": "BOOK_NARROWS", "extension_relation": "BOOK_SUBSET", "boundary_disagreement": "The book sharpens the consensus's general 'sin/corruption/false teaching' into a doctrinal specification: leaven is essentially the corruption of the word (bread = the word, so soured bread = the word made impure). This makes false doctrine the defining core rather than one prominent application among general moral corruption. The book also silently omits the widely recognized positive kingdom-parable reading (Matt 13:33) and the neutral/positive OT cases (Lev 7:13; 23:17), implying a uniformly negative symbolism — aligning with the consensus's noted minority 'always negative' position.", "material_contradiction": "None at the core. The book's identification (corrupt doctrine that ferments through the whole) is contained within the consensus's negative primary sense; Matt 16:12 explicitly supports the doctrinal identification. The tightening to 'the word made impure' and the implicit exclusion of the positive kingdom reading are boundary moves, not a replacement of the referent.", "rationale": "Both readings identify leaven as hidden, pervasive corruption purged at Passover and exemplified by Pharisaic teaching. The book preserves this central referent but materially changes precision and boundary: it derives the symbol from bread=word (making doctrinal impurity the essence rather than one instance of general sin/hypocrisy), and it treats leaven as uniformly negative, effectively rejecting the common positive reading of the kingdom parable that the consensus admits. This is real disagreement at the boundary within the same category, so REFINED rather than MATCH; there is no contradiction of the central identification, so not DIVERGENT.", "citation_support": "PARTIAL", "strongest_objection": "One could argue MATCH: the consensus's primary meaning already lists 'false teaching' prominently, Matt 16:12 explicitly equates leaven with doctrine, and the book's phrase 'hidden corruption that ferments through the whole lump' echoes the general consensus wording — so the doctrinal emphasis may be immaterial detail rather than a genuine narrowing. Against this, the 'bread soured = the word made impure' derivation is a distinctive systematic claim (dependent on bread symbolizing the word) that the printed citations do not themselves establish, and the entry's silence on the positive kingdom usage marks a real boundary difference.", "confidence": "medium"}
